text:
Vasily Podkolzin became a folk hero in Edmonton this week. After Anaheim's Drew Helleson ran Connor McDavid into the post, Podkolzin went after him and was ejected with a game misconduct (Sportsnet), and the Edmonton Journal reported support for him from across Canada. Oilersnation called him "an absolute rockstar." The hockey has earned him that platform too. He has nine goals and 14 points in 17 games, on pace far above last season's 0.45 points a game, and the Oilers control almost 62% of the 5v5 chances with him on, 20 points better than without him.

This is a real breakout with some air in it. He is playing 17:34 a night, up from 15:23, and is on the ice for 40% of Edmonton's power-play chances after 12% last year, and his own chances are up to 1.21 expected goals per 60 from 0.78. But he is shooting 26% (14% last season) and his teammates are scoring 5.6 goals above their chances with him out there. Over the last ten games he has five points, and his recent ice time has dipped. Our projection has him around 27 goals: a big year, not a 40-goal one.
headline: Podkolzin's breakout, and the night he became a hero
